newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian labour min sees hope for metal dispute.
newsitem.headline: Italian labour min sees hope for metal dispute.

text.p: Italian Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said on Wednesday there were signs of hope that the deadlock in the long-running dispute in the metalworkers and engineering sector might soon be broken.

"The climate is very uncertain, but the prospects are for better weather at the end of the week," Treu, speaking in English, told a press conference. "We're beginning to see something moving," he added.

Employers group Federmeccanica reaffirmed on Tuesday that it would not accept a government proposal aimed at ending the six month pay row. Treu suggested in December that management should offer workers a pay rise of 200,000 lire per month.
Unions, which wanted 230,000 lire, accepted the proposal but employers have stuck to their 139,000 lire offer.
Treu did not give any details of how a breakthrough might be achieved.
Federmeccanica director general Michele Figurati said on Tuesday he didn't know if, how or when the negotiations would be unblocked. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
